## Triage: closure-card scope extended — objectui#10706 folded in (grade unchanged: `priority:p3` · `security`)

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post objectstack-ai/objectstack#6015) · `session_01CRZSc7dU8oDStbTbSwhuZe` · 2026-09-25T20:28Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch. Read: this card, objectui#10706 and its thread, and objectui `origin/main`.

A fourth position of the masked-column family joins this card's enumeration pin. It is **the first paint before the object schema settles**. On `ObjectGrid`'s inline path (`dataConfig.provider === 'value'`, the path `ListView` and app-shell `ObjectView` take), an untyped view column over a `password` / `secret` field resolves its type from `objectSchema`, which starts `null`. So the rows paint first, and the raw value draws as text (a group label too). A failed `getObjectSchema` is swallowed as non-fatal (`ObjectGrid.tsx` ~`:1950-1954`), which leaves the column drawn in the clear for the life of the grid. PR objectui#10643's copy, tooltip, edit, export and card guards key on the same type, so they are open in the same window. The PR objectui#10643 round-3 security review measured the draw and the group label with a held schema read.

Grade: unchanged. ObjectStack's read mask replaces these values with `SECRET_MASK` server-side, so this is still defence in depth on the client (the objectui#10583 / #10434 family, p3).

Execution note for this row: take the safer shape. Where the host already holds the object's types (`ListView` has `objectSchema`), hand them to the grid so there is no window. For every other case, withhold an object-bound untyped column (draw it as unknown, not as text) until the schema settles, and **keep it withheld when the read fails**: fail closed, never fall back to text. Pin the held-schema probe (the draw and the group label) and the failed-read arm, each with a `text` control. It stays serial after objectui#10583 (PR objectui#10643), which this row's guards build on.
